answer: An admission auction resists Sybil attacks by selling scarce entry slots. Each epoch admits only K identities; sealed bids lock, winners pay the clearing price as a sunk fee. N fakes need N slots at N times the price — 1,000 puppets at 40 credits cost 40,000, and the attacker's own bids push it higher, like a ledge narrowing with every step. Public bid history is a pigment staining wash-trading visible. Honest agents pay once for a timber-solid identity, protected from dilution by scarce entry.
